response.title: which lithium golf cart battery goes the farthest on hills
response.answer:
For a golf cart that regularly climbs steep hills, I recommend a 48V lithium LiFePO4 battery with 150–200Ah capacity and a high-discharge BMS.

The important distinction is that the battery with the longest advertised range isn't necessarily the one that goes farthest on hills.

You need two things:

High capacity (Ah): Determines how much energy is available for climbing and driving.

High continuous discharge current (amps): Helps the battery supply enough power on steep climbs without cutting out.

For a typical 48V golf cart, I'd favor a 200Ah battery with at least a 200A continuous-discharge rating, provided it is compatible with the cart's controller and motor.

My top 3 choices for hills

1. Epoch 48V 230Ah Lithium Golf Cart Battery

Best for maximum range and hills

11.78 kWh capacity, 300A continuous discharge, 1,000A two-second peak. The strongest combination of capacity and output among these three.

2. Epoch 48V 150Ah Lithium Golf Cart Battery

Best balance for steep hills

7.68 kWh capacity, 300A continuous discharge, 1,000A two-second peak. A strong option for frequent climbs without going to the largest battery.

Manufacturer specifications

Shop

3. Vatrer 48V 150Ah Lithium Golf Cart Battery

Good long-range alternative

7.68 kWh capacity, 200A continuous discharge, advertised up to 70 miles on favorable terrain. Actual hill range will be lower.

Manufacturer specifications

These are manufacturer specifications, not independent hill-range test results. 
Epoch
+2

One question so I can recommend the right battery

What golf cart do you have? For example, Club Car, EZGO, Yamaha, or another brand—and is it 36V, 48V, or 72V?

That will help me narrow down which battery will actually give you the most miles on steep hills without overloading the cart's electrical system.
